messages:
tara: hey everyone, I'm Tara, just started today in Infra. Quick Q: what's the best channel to ask about laptop VPN, Okta MFA access, and badge provisioning?

matt: welcome Tara! For HR/badge stuff open a ticket in #help-access and cc @people-ops. For infra creds use #eng-infra (short message + link to the ticket). If it's blocking your work today, ping @sre-oncall.

jess: +1. For hardware/monitor requests use the hardware request form linked in #eng-infra pinned messages.

onboard-bot: Welcome Tara! To kick off your checklist run: `/onboard start tara@redwood.ai`. Pinned: onboarding checklist + FAQ.

tara: thanks! also—where do people post "can someone review my PR" or "quick design sign-off needed"? #eng or #product?

matt: PR review requests should live in the PR, but drop a one-line in #eng with the PR link and reviewer @mention if you want a faster turnaround. Product/UX signoffs -> #product-review or tag the PM on the PR.

jess: etiquette tips: 1) use threads for follow-ups, 2) use :thumbsup: reactions to ACK instead of "got it", 3) avoid @channel for individual asks. Keep messages short & link to context.

sre-oncall: FYI — only page oncall for production incidents. For perf/latency questions post in #eng-sre with a concise summary + traces/logs. Example: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/trace -d '{"span":"xyz"}'```

tara: where should we ask about bots like remind-bot and standup-bot?

matt: bot admin/config questions -> #devex. Use `/remind` sparingly, and never use @channel for routine reminders. If a bot is noisy, file an issue in #devex and ping @devex-team.

ci-bot: To subscribe to build notifications: `/ci subscribe repo-name --channel #eng-releases`. Use filters to avoid noise.

jess: extra tip — use the People directory or `@people-bot search "infra"` in DMs to find owners quickly. Check a channel's pinned messages before asking to avoid duplicates.

tara: awesome — last one: lunch invites and social stuff?

matt: #lunch-plans for team meals, #random for memes/watercooler. If it's a team-wide event, a short post in #general is fine but prefer scheduled calendar invites. Welcome aboard :party_parrot:
